Name: Fishing Reborn
Author: xzqute
Description:
[center][size=4][img]https://i.imgur.com/lIyzY2Q.png[/img]
[img]https://img.shields.io/badge/SMAPI-4.5.2+-brightgreen.svg[/img] [img]https://img.shields.io/badge/Stardew%20Valley-1.6.15+-orange.svg[/img] [img]https://img.shields.io/badge/GMCM-Optional-purple.svg[/img]
Pull against the fish's runs, and take a breather before it wears you out.[/size][/center]

[b][size=4]Fishing Reborn[/size][/b][size=4] replaces the fishing bar with a fight in the water. You can watch the fish approach your bait and follow it beneath the surface once it's hooked, with the bobber moving along behind it. Pull against its runs to tire it out, take breaks to recover your grip, and bring it back into the circle for the final pull.[/size]

[size=4]A Catfish makes a second run just as you start to relax after the first. An Eel follows a winding path through the water. Legendary fish have abilities you'll need to work around. You can prepare with groundbait and tackle, but once a fish is on the line, you'll need to watch what it does.[/size]

[size=5][b]Fishing in the world[/b][/size]

[size=4]While you wait for a bite, a silhouette swims toward the bait. You still need to wait for the real bite signal before hooking it. During the fight, the fish stays beneath the surface, with the bobber and line following its movements. Where available, fish use their aquarium sprites and swimming animations.[/size]

[size=4]The circle stays where the fight began. Outside it, the risk of escape builds until you pull the fish back. You get a little help pulling inward near the edge. Fish also stay within connected water and turn along the banks when they reach the shore.[/size]

[size=5][b]Learn their habits[/b][/size]

[size=4]Some fish drift quietly before a sudden straight run. Others sweep around you or change sides, and a pause after one burst doesn't always mean they're finished.[/size]

[b][size=4]20 species have their own movement patterns:[/size][/b][size=4] the 19 fish from the standard Fish Tank bundles, plus Chub from the Field Research Bundle. Catfish run in two directions before resting. Sardines make three small runs, while Eels follow an S-shaped path. Tilapia reverse their arcs, and Sturgeon follow a long straight run with a short sideways escape.[/size]
[center][/center]
[center][img]https://i.imgur.com/gjTPLLo.png[/img][/center]

[size=4]The other ordinary fish use five movement profiles, with outward runs, sidesteps, and feints between quieter stretches. Nearby banks affect their tactics. They can also respond to low grip or a pull you've held in the same direction for too long.[/size]

[b][size=4]All 20 individual patterns[/size][/b]
[spoiler][list]
[*][size=4][b]Sunfish:[/b] a broad arc followed by a short straight run.[/size][/*]
[/list][list]
[*][size=4][b]Catfish:[/b] two runs in different directions, then a long rest.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Shad:[/b] two parallel bursts in the same direction.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Tiger Trout:[/b] a straight run and a diagonal escape, switching the diagonal between cycles.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Largemouth Bass:[/b] a wide sideways approach followed by an outward run.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Carp:[/b] gentle, broad arcs with occasional straight bursts and long pauses.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Bullhead:[/b] runs away from the angler, alternating straight and slightly sideways headings.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Sturgeon:[/b] a long straight run followed by a short lateral escape.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Sardine:[/b] three small runs with alternating sides, then a longer pause.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Tuna:[/b] long straight passes to either side of the direction away from the angler.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Red Snapper:[/b] a pair of diagonal bursts in opposite lateral directions.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Tilapia:[/b] curved runs that reverse their circling direction between cycles.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Walleye:[/b] a long quiet stretch before a short straight burst.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Bream:[/b] a short sideways escape followed by a longer, shallow curve.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Eel:[/b] an S-shaped path during its run.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Pufferfish:[/b] slow movement between short outward bursts.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Ghostfish:[/b] a faint drift and gentle turns that alternate sides.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Sandfish:[/b] two straight runs, with the second angled away from the first.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Woodskip:[/b] diagonal runs relative to the angler, turning along nearby banks.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Chub:[/b] a short straight run and a longer curved one, with small arcs between them.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]Every burst gets its own warning, including the later runs in a pair or a group of three.[/size][/spoiler]

[size=5][b]Legendary fish[/b][/size]

[size=4]All [/size][b][size=4]10 legendary fish[/size][/b][size=4] have their own rhythms and abilities. Changes in the water, fishing line, and pull indicator give you clues about what they're doing.[/size]

[size=4]That includes the original five and their Extended Family counterparts. The spoilers below explain each fight if you get stuck or want to know what to expect.[/size]

[b][size=4][img]https://i.imgur.com/yzd26BG.png[/img] Glacierfish[/size][/b]
[spoiler][size=4]Glacierfish makes long, straight bursts and rests for a while afterward. During the warning, your pull indicator turns blue; during the burst, it turns at only 25% of its usual speed.

Set your direction before the freeze takes hold. Use the recovery period to turn freely and restore grip before the next run.[/size][/spoiler]
[size=4][b][img]https://i.imgur.com/fnOaZDm.png[/img] Crimsonfish[/b][/size]
[spoiler][size=4]Crimsonfish alternates sideways runs with an outward push. Pulling continuously heats the line, and preparing an attack adds more heat. The line changes color as it heats up; at full heat, pulling uses 70% more grip.

Release the pull button to cool the line. Its long rests after attacks give you time to cool down and recover before the next burst.[/size][/spoiler]
[size=4][b][img]https://i.imgur.com/zCFBeCm.png[/img] Angler[/b][/size]
[spoiler][size=4]Angler starts with a slow feint, then reads your pull direction and prepares its real burst in that direction. The real attack still gets a full bubble warning.

Let the feint play out, then use the real warning to redirect your pull against the announced burst. If you keep pulling the same way, you'll help it escape.[/size][/spoiler]
[size=4][b][img]https://i.imgur.com/9t2iN9P.png[/img] Mutant Carp[/b][/size]
[spoiler][size=4]Mutant Carp leaves slime trails during its curved outward runs. Slime remains for several seconds, so the previous trail can still be active when a new one appears. Inside slime, the fish's endurance recovery is tripled.

Draw it into clean water and keep pressure on it there. Chasing it along its own trail gives it more opportunity to recover.[/size][/spoiler]
[size=4][b][img]https://i.imgur.com/lUYNc7V.png[/img] Legend[/b][/size]
[spoiler][size=4]Legend circles between attacks, then curves outward during its runs. Small whirlpools appear in the fishing area. If your pull indicator enters one, the current takes over its direction and rotates it until it leaves the field or the whirlpool ends.

You can release the pull button while the indicator is caught to save grip. Steering returns gradually when it comes free, so allow for that before committing to another pull.[/size][/spoiler]
[size=4][b][img]https://i.imgur.com/dlk5aM8.png[/img] Glacierfish Jr.[/b][/size]
[spoiler][size=4]Glacierfish Jr. makes two short bursts with a brief break between them. Each burst freezes your pull indicator and slows its turning, just like Glacierfish. The indicator thaws between attacks.

Use that brief thaw to prepare for the second burst. Save longer rests for the pause after the pair.[/size][/spoiler]
[size=4][b][img]https://i.imgur.com/i9nQynk.png[/img] Son of Crimsonfish[/b][/size]
[spoiler][size=4]Son of Crimsonfish makes pairs of quick sideways runs. The first run leaves a patch of hot water, marked by bubbles, for five seconds. If it prepares the next attack inside that patch, the burst becomes stronger.

Steer it away from the bubbling patch before the next warning begins. Use the longer pause after the pair to recover grip.[/size][/spoiler]
[size=4][b][img]https://i.imgur.com/8KfFcTM.png[/img] Ms. Angler[/b][/size]
[spoiler][size=4]Ms. Angler reads your pull direction and curves around to flank you. Changing your pull direction substantially from the direction it read weakens the attack by 20%, provided you are actively pulling with enough grip.

Reposition during the warning, then pull against its burst. Small adjustments will not fool it; you need a clear change of direction.[/size][/spoiler]
[size=4][b][img]https://i.imgur.com/meXQcdf.png[/img] Radioactive Carp[/b][/size]
[spoiler][size=4]Radioactive Carp makes short bursts with little cruising time between attacks. The fish and bobber shake more as its charge builds. Unless suppressed, that charge triples its endurance recovery for the first 0.75 seconds after the burst.

A successful counter-pull during the burst suppresses the charge. You can also stop the recovery surge by pulling firmly against the announced burst direction as the pulse begins. After suppressing it, take your break.[/size][/spoiler]
[size=4][b][img]https://i.imgur.com/nswEmas.png[/img] Legend II[/b][/size]
[spoiler][size=4]Legend II makes pairs of curved outward bursts on alternating sides. Its whirlpools change their spin direction between attacks. These whirlpools push the fish sideways while it is inside them. You keep control of your pull indicator.

Compensate for the sideways current and pull the fish out of the whirlpool. Stay ready for the second burst before taking a longer rest.[/size][/spoiler]

[size=5][b]When to pull[/b][/size]

[size=4]Pulling uses grip, shown by the lightning bolt beside your farmer. Release the button between pulls to recover, and try to save some for the next run. If you use it all, you'll briefly lose the ability to pull. Grip is a temporary reserve for the fight, separate from your farmer's regular energy.[/size]

[size=4]Bubbles show which way the fish will burst. Take a short break, then pull the opposite way as it launches. Get the timing right and you'll land a [/size][b][size=4]counter-pull[/size][/b][size=4], briefly tiring the fish faster while using less grip. Changing direction at the right moment can also trigger it. Counter-pulls help with harder catches, though you can land a fish without them.[/size]

[size=4]Once the fish is tired and inside the circle, an icon and sound tell you it's ready to land. Make the [/size][b][size=4]final pull[/size][/b][size=4] to bring it in. An early attempt makes it resist.[/size]

[b][size=4]Exact timing and bonuses[/size][/b]
[spoiler][size=4]The landing icon appears at 20% fish endurance or below, while the fish is inside the circle.

For a counter-pull, rest for at least 0.15 seconds during the warning, then begin pulling against the burst within its opening window. A timely change of direction also works. The direction tolerance is 45 degrees. The window is 0.65 seconds in Relax, 0.35 in Standard, and 0.2 in Hardcore.

A successful counter grants one second of advantage: correctly opposed pulling tires the fish 50% faster and grip use falls by 25%.[/size][/spoiler]

[size=5][b]Prepare a fishing spot[/b][/size]

[size=4]Craft some groundbait and select it in your toolbar. Hold the usual Use Tool button to prepare the throw, then release it to send the ball into the water. Crumbs scatter beneath the surface and sway in the water. They thin out as you use the spot, while Glitter Groundbait casts a warm light at night.[/size]

[size=4]Each blend helps with a different part of fishing:[/size]

[b][size=4][img]https://i.imgur.com/errrJjp.png[/img] Grain Groundbait[/size][/b]
[size=4]Shortens the wait for a bite.[/size]

[b][size=4][img]https://i.imgur.com/yzULfUe.png[/img]Select Groundbait[/size][/b]
[size=4]Gives catches a chance at better starting quality.[/size]

[b][size=4][img]https://i.imgur.com/kklVN4S.png[/img] Hearty Groundbait[/size][/b]
[size=4]Helps tire a fish faster when you pull against its movement.[/size]

[b][size=4][img]https://i.imgur.com/x3zSqmp.png[/img] Calming Groundbait[/size][/b]
[size=4]Lengthens the warning before a burst, giving you more time to line up a counter-pull.[/size]

[b][size=4][img]https://i.imgur.com/49orJ26.png[/img] Glitter Groundbait[/size][/b]
[size=4]Gives you another chance to find treasure. You'll still need to collect the chest during the fight.[/size]

[size=4]Each patch covers a two-tile radius and lasts for [/size][b][size=4]five successful catches or two in-game hours[/size][/b][size=4]. Throwing into an existing patch refreshes it; a different blend replaces its effect. Only one blend applies at a time; the bonuses don't stack. Recipes unlock with Fishing skill and make two balls each.[/size]

[b][size=4]Groundbait recipes and exact effects[/size][/b]
[spoiler][list]
[*][size=4][b]Grain, Fishing 2:[/b] Wheat x1 + Fiber x3. Bite waiting time is reduced by 30%.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Select, Fishing 4:[/b] Wheat Flour x1 + Maple Syrup x1 + Green Algae x1. A 35% chance to raise base quality by one tier, capped at gold. The Training Rod's quality restriction still applies.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Hearty, Fishing 5:[/b] Bug Meat x1 + Sap x2 + Wheat x1. Correctly opposed pulls tire the fish 25% faster.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Calming, Fishing 6:[/b] Seaweed x1 + Honey x1 + Fiber x3. Pre-burst warnings last 40% longer, including the built-in legendary patterns.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Glitter, Fishing 7:[/b] Quartz x1 + Copper Ore x1 + Sap x2. If the normal treasure roll produces no chest, there is an independent 25% chance to add one. This is not an extra 25 percentage points on the final treasure chance. Normal treasure eligibility and golden chest rules still apply.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]Existing saves receive recipes they already qualify for. A failed or cancelled catch does not consume a patch charge. A Challenge Bait multi-catch uses one charge. The patch's effect is chosen when the bobber lands and stays with that cast even if the patch expires during the fight.[/size][/spoiler]

[size=5][b]Worm bait[/b][/size]

[b][size=4][img]https://i.imgur.com/Fr9v3g6.png[/img] Worm bait[/size][/b]

[size=4]You can find worms while tilling fresh soil, with better odds in the rain. Attach them to your rod's normal bait slot.[/size]

[size=4]Worms shorten the wait for bites and sometimes replace an ordinary catch with a fish of higher base value available in that spot. They also improve the chance of a legendary bite when its usual requirements are met.[/size]

[b][size=4]Worm drop rates and bait bonuses[/size][/b]
[spoiler][size=4]Each freshly tilled tile has a 10% chance to drop a worm, rising to 20% if it is raining in that location. After a successful drop, there is a separate 5% chance to receive two worms. An upgraded hoe checks each newly tilled tile; hitting existing tilled soil or watering does not produce worms.

Worm bait reduces the bite wait by a further 25% compared with ordinary bait. On an eligible ordinary catch, it has a 25% chance to select an available fish with a higher base price. If no suitable upgrade exists, the original catch stays. Seasons, weather, time, location, skill requirements, and catch limits still apply.

Legendary bite probability is multiplied by 1.15, a relative 15% increase rather than 15 percentage points. Ordinary fish do not become legendaries through the price upgrade. Legendary catches, the tutorial catch, Fish Ponds, fish frenzies, and flagged special rewards are excluded from that upgrade. Bait consumption follows the game's rules, including Preserving.[/size][/spoiler]

[size=5][b]Treasure and effect tiles[/b][/size]

[size=4]To collect a chest, steer the tired fish onto its tile and make the final pull there. You'll bring in both together. If the fish runs out of endurance, the chest starts sinking, so plan your approach before the end of the fight.[/size]

[size=4]Temporary effect tiles can appear in the water during a fight. Yellow tiles increase the fish's swimming force; orange tiles reduce it. Steer a difficult fish through an orange tile for some help, and watch out if it's heading toward a yellow one.[/size]

[b][size=4]Effect values[/size][/b]
[spoiler][size=4]Yellow tiles increase swimming force by 30%; orange tiles reduce it by 30%. Both last 2.5 seconds after contact and replace the previous speed effect. They affect the fish's swimming force, not your pull strength.[/size][/spoiler]

[size=5][b]Skill and tackle[/b][/size]

[size=4]Higher Fishing skill gives you more grip for longer pulls. Skill and equipment bonuses that normally increase fishing-bar size expand the circle instead.[/size]

[size=4]Tackle is adapted to the new minigame:[/size]
[list]
[*][size=4][b]Cork Bobber[/b] expands the fishing circle.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Trap Bobber[/b] slows the risk of escape while the fish is outside it.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Lead Bobber[/b] smooths changes in your pull.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Barbed Hook[/b] helps with steering.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Treasure Hunter[/b] makes the chest's catch area larger.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Sonar Bobber[/b] reveals the fish's colors beneath the water.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]
Auto-Hook still handles the initial hook when a real bite arrives. Challenge Bait also carries over: control mistakes and premature landing attempts can cost you fish from the catch. The game continues to handle catch rewards, XP, quests, quality, and bait consumption, with the groundbait and worm bonuses described above applied where relevant.

[b]Skill bonus[/b][/size]
[spoiler][size=4]Each effective Fishing level adds 5% of the base grip capacity, including food buffs and Master, up to effective level 20. This gives up to 100% additional capacity. Tackle does not multiply this grip bonus. A larger reserve also takes longer to refill completely.[/size][/spoiler]

[size=5][b]Find your own pace[/b][/size]

[size=4]Before your first cast, an [/size][b][size=4]illustrated tutorial[/size][/b][size=4] takes you from the bite to the final pull. It covers grip, countering bursts, the circle, effect tiles, and treasure, then lets you choose difficulty and assistance. You can skip it and return later with [/size][b][size=4]fr_guide[/size][/b][size=4] in the SMAPI console.[/size]

[size=4]There are three difficulty presets:[/size]
[list]
[*][size=4][b]Relax[/b] gives you gentler fish, longer warnings, and more time to bring a wandering catch back.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Standard[/b] is the default, with time to learn the patterns while keeping an eye on the fish.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Hardcore[/b] demands quicker responses and more careful use of your grip. Bring developed Fishing skill and strong equipment for the difficult catches.[/size][/*]
[/list][b][size=4]Automatic pull direction[/size][/b][size=4] handles steering while you decide when to pull, rest, and land. [/size][b][size=4]Toggle pulling[/size][/b][size=4] lets you press once to start and again to stop. Turning speed, inversion, keybinds, and controller dead zone can be adjusted too.[/size]

[size=4]Reduced motion, high contrast, fewer decorative effects, sound, and vibration have their own settings. Essential warnings and legendary hazards stay visible with fewer effects enabled.[/size]

[size=4]You can use [/size][b][size=4]Skip[/size][/b][size=4] to land a fish immediately. Skipped catches are capped at silver quality and award neither Perfect nor treasure.[/size]

[size=5][b]Controls[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][size=4][b]Hook:[/b] your usual Use Tool button after the bite signal.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Pull:[/b] hold Left Mouse / Space, or X on a controller. Release to rest.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Aim:[/b] mouse, WASD, arrow keys, left stick, or D-pad.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Final pull / collect chest:[/b] Right Mouse / F, or controller A, when the landing icon appears.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Cancel:[/b] Escape or controller B.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4][b]Free the game cursor:[/b] hold Alt during the fight.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=5][b]Installation and settings[/b][/size]
[list=1]
[*][size=4]Use Stardew Valley [b]1.6.15 or newer[/b] and install [url=https://smapi.io/]SMAPI[/url] [b]4.5.2 or newer[/b].[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Extract the download into [b]Stardew Valley/Mods[/b]. The archive contains the [b]FishingReborn[/b] folder.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Launch through SMAPI and load your save. The welcome screen appears before your first cast with the mod enabled.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Optional: install [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url] to adjust settings in game. Without it, you can edit config.json; the tutorial also provides the main difficulty and assistance options.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=5][b]Compatibility and feedback[/b][/size]

[size=4]Developed against [/size][b][size=4]Stardew Valley 1.6.15 build 24356[/size][/b][size=4] and [/size][b][size=4]SMAPI 4.5.2[/size][/b][size=4] on Windows x64. Other builds and operating systems have not been verified.[/size]

[size=4]Mods that replace the fishing minigame or automate catches may need an adapter. When a conflicting fishing patch or an unsupported situation is detected, Fishing Reborn falls back to vanilla fishing. Custom fish and maps need testing with their individual mods; multiplayer, split-screen, and festival behavior still need live verification.[/size]

[size=4]For bug reports, include your SMAPI log, mod version, and steps to reproduce the issue. A screenshot or short clip helps with visual or control problems. Feedback on how the fish feel to catch is useful too, especially when a pattern is hard to read or a difficulty setting leaves too little room to respond.[/size]

Downloads.Description: Reworked fishing with directional pulling, stamina management, and timed counters. Includes distinct fish behaviors, legendary abilities, groundbait, and a built-in tutorial.

Manifest.Name: Fishing Reborn
Manifest.Description: Fishing in Stardew Valley is now a fight to land your catch. Watch how the fish moves, take breaks between pulls to recover stamina, and time your final pull to reel it in. Legendary fish have their own unique abilities to deal with.
Manifest.Author: xzqute
